entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:10, when they saw the Egyptians, the Israelites got ready for battle.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Observe the people's fear in the face of the army.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: They don't get ready to fight: they are terrified and cry out to the Lord.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of Exodus 14:10: the people were terrified and cried out to the Lord.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Look at the people's reaction at the end of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:16, tap what Moses must lift up.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Observe the gesture the Lord asks of Moses.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: Moses lifts his staff and stretches out his hand over the sea, as the Lord commands.

feedbackWrong.b: "mar" (sea) is what Moses stretches his hand over; he lifts something else.
feedbackWrong.c: "filhos" (the Israelites) are the ones who will cross, not what Moses lifts.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Look for the object Moses holds in his hands.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.question: According to Exodus 14:11–12, what do the people say to Moses?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Observe the people's complaint in the face of danger.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: Afraid, the people would rather be slaves in Egypt than die in the wilderness.

feedbackWrong.a: The people don't speak of trust; they accuse Moses of bringing them out to die.
feedbackWrong.c: No one talks about fighting; the people want to go back to serving the Egyptians.
feedbackWrong.d: The people don't even know about the crossing yet; they're complaining about leaving Egypt.

options.a: That they trusted God would deliver them
options.b: That it was better to serve the Egyptians than to die
options.c: That they wanted to fight against Pharaoh
options.d: That they were ready to cross the sea

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.question: Put Exodus 14:10 in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: That's the verse's sequence: the people look up, see the Egyptians and are filled with fear.

feedbackWrong.default: First the people lift their eyes; the fear comes after they see the Egyptians.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Before being afraid, the people need to see something.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:16, how would the Israelites pass through the middle of the sea?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Remember how the people would cross the sea.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: The sea opens and the people cross on foot, on dry ground.

feedbackWrong.b: The text doesn't mention a "fila" (line); it speaks of the ground the people walk on.
feedbackWrong.c: There are no "barcos" (boats): the sea is divided and the people cross on foot.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Think about the ground the people will walk on.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.question: What does Exodus 14:14 communicate that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Connect the promise of 14:14 to the danger the people faced.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: Facing an army, the people don't fight: the Lord fights for them.

feedbackWrong.a: The people don't take up arms; the verse says they will keep silent.
feedbackWrong.b: Moses doesn't fight; he announces that the Lord will fight.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: See who is the subject of the verb "lutará".

options.c: The Lord fights for the people

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:14, the people and the Lord share the fight against the Egyptians.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the Lord's action and the people's.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: There's no sharing: the Lord fights, and the people keep silent.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Exodus 14:14: the fight belongs to the Lord alone; the people are to keep silent.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Compare the Lord's part with the people's part.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:13, tap the word that marks the contrast between the people's complaint and Moses' reply.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Recognize the marker that separates the people's fear from Moses' word.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" turns the scene: the people want to go back, but Moses tells them to stand firm.

feedbackWrong.a: "Porque" gives a reason; the contrast comes at the start of the verse.
feedbackWrong.b: "Hoje" says when the Lord will act; it doesn't mark a contrast.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Look for a short word between commas, right after Moses' name.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.question: How does Moses' answer in Exodus 14:13 respond to the people's complaint in 14:12?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Understand Moses' answer as a contrast to the people's complaint.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: The people say they'll die; Moses answers: don't fear, see what the Lord will do today.

feedbackWrong.a: There's no negotiation; Moses points to what the Lord will do.
feedbackWrong.b: Moses goes the opposite way: the people must not go back, but see the deliverance.
feedbackWrong.d: Moses doesn't mention weapons; he tells the people to be still.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Compare the fear in 14:12 with Moses' first command.

options.a: He asks the people to negotiate peace with Pharaoh
options.b: He agrees it was better to go back to Egypt
options.c: He trades fear for trust in what the Lord will do
options.d: He tells the people to take up arms against Pharaoh

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.question: How does the scene move forward in Exodus 14:15–16?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Understand the movement from God's command to the opened path.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: First the Lord interrupts the cry, then tells them to move on, and then opens the way.

feedbackWrong.default: The path through the sea comes last; before that, the Lord speaks and tells the people to go on.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: The open path is the end point.

options.a: The people are told to move forward
options.b: The staff over the sea opens the way

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:14, what will the Lord do for the people?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Remember the Lord's action that changes the scene.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: The battle is the Lord's: he acts, and the people only need to trust.

feedbackWrong.b: "Esperará" (will wait) doesn't fit: the Lord doesn't sit and wait; he acts for the people.
feedbackWrong.c: "Orará" (will pray) doesn't fit: the people are the ones who cry out; the Lord answers by acting.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: It's the action the Lord takes in the people's place.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.question: What connects Exodus 14:17 to Psalm 106:8?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Relate the deliverance at the sea to God's glory in the Psalms.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, the deliverance reveals the Lord's power and glory.

feedbackWrong.a: The psalm says God saved them "for his name's sake", not because the people deserved it.
feedbackWrong.b: Neither text speaks of Pharaoh repenting; they speak of God's glory.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Compare why God acts in each text.

options.a: The people are saved because they deserve it
options.c: God saves and shows who he is

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.question: Exodus 14:13–14 presents the deliverance as the Lord's work, not as the people's achievement.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Interpret the exodus as salvation that comes from God.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: The people only watch and keep silent; the Lord is the one who delivers and fights.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 14:13–14: the deliverance is "do Senhor", and he is the one who fights for the people.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Look at whose deliverance it is and who does the fighting.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:15, tap the phrase that shows that being still doesn't mean staying put.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Support from the text that trusting is not standing still.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: Trusting the Lord includes obeying: the quieted people are told to move forward.

feedbackWrong.a: "Clama a mim" is about Moses' cry, not about what the people must do.
feedbackWrong.b: "Por que" opens the Lord's question; the command to the people comes at the end.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Look for the command given to the Israelites.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.question: What reading does Exodus 14:14–15 support about the people's role in the deliverance?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about faith and obedience.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: The Lord fights; the people stop despairing and move forward when God commands.

feedbackWrong.a: The people had just complained and wanted to go back; deliverance is grace, not a reward.
feedbackWrong.b: Right after "calarão", the Lord tells the people to move forward.
feedbackWrong.d: The people were afraid; the text says the Lord would fight for them.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Read both verses together: what is the Lord's part and what is the people's.

options.a: The people were saved because they deserved it
options.b: Being still means waiting idly, doing nothing
options.c: The people trust the Lord and obey when he commands
options.d: The people were saved for being brave and fighting well

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.question: Which sequence shows the Bible returning to the deliverance at the sea?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: See the exodus as the picture of salvation that the Bible repeats.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: The exodus (Exod 14) is recalled by the prophets (Isa 43:16) and fulfilled in Christ (1 Cor 5:7).

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: the parted sea, the prophets who recall it, and Christ who brings the greater deliverance.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: Follow the Bible's order: Exodus, the prophets, the NT letters.

options.a: Isaiah recalls the God who made a way through the sea
options.b: Paul calls Christ our Passover Lamb
options.c: The Lord divides the sea and Israel crosses on dry ground

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.question: In Exodus 14:13, what must the people see the Lord accomplish?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Remember the term that sums up God's work in the exodus.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: It is salvation worked by the Lord: the people don't win it, they only see and receive it.

feedbackWrong.b: God's "poder" (power) will show, but Moses speaks of the salvation the people will receive.
feedbackWrong.c: There will be "juízo" (judgment) on the Egyptians, but Moses speaks of what the Lord will do for them.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: It's the word that sums up what God does for the people in this scene.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.question: What connects Exodus 14:16 to 1 Corinthians 10:1–2?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.learningObjective: Connect the crossing of the sea to the way the NT reads it.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.feedbackCorrect: Paul reads the crossing as a figure of baptism: all passed through the sea and were baptized.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul insists on "all": all of them crossed the sea.
feedbackWrong.c: Paul doesn't speak of a battle; he speaks of the whole people passing through the sea.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-04-.hint: See what Paul says happened "in the cloud and in the sea".

options.a: Only the strong crossed the sea
options.b: The crossing as a picture of baptism

estudo:entrada-biblia-04.context: Abraham's descendants became slaves in Egypt. After the plagues, Pharaoh lets the people go, but soon changes his mind and goes after them with his army. Israel is trapped between the soldiers and the sea.
estudo:entrada-biblia-04.focusQuestion: In what situation do you need to stop fighting alone and see what the Lord will do?
estudo:entrada-biblia-04.keywordGloss: The salvation that comes from the Lord when the people have no way to save themselves.
facts: When they saw the Egyptians, the Israelites were terrified and cried out to the Lord.
The people tell Moses it would be better to serve the Egyptians.
Moses tells the people not to fear and to see the Lord's deliverance.
Moses says the Lord will fight for the people.
The Lord tells the people to move forward.
The sea would be divided so the people could cross on dry ground.
